messages:
maria: Heads up — after the RBAC roll yesterday we're seeing a ~5x spike in audit events for policy checks. Narrow question: do we want to expand the schema to keep full policy document in each event, or normalize and reference via policy_id?

sam: Thanks for flagging. I vote normalize -> policy_id only. storing full policy JSON per event will blow storage and indexing. :thumbsup:

maria: +1 on normalize. main concern: customers expect policy snapshots in customer-facing audit events (for compliance). can we provide on-demand expansion for e-Discovery?

jason: We can keep a denormalized snapshot table (S3 parquet) per policy version and include policy_version in the event. Event contains policy_id + version -> lookup when customer requests. cheap to store and avoids hot ES index.

katie: For customer-facing validation we also need signed hashes so customers can verify we didn't alter events. That ties into KMS question — each signature currently uses a KMS sign call. Cost and latency?

maria: Exactly. KMS per-event adds latency and $$$. Proposal: use envelope signing: local HMAC with a rotating DEK (data-encryption-key), and store DEK encrypted with KMS once per rotation window. That way KMS calls are O(rotation) not O(event).

sam: Agreed. Also consider switching heavy audit -> append-only blob (compressed) + periodic index for search. For high-throughput tenants, we can sample low-sensitivity events at 1% for indexing and keep full archive for compliance retention.

jason: From ingestion side, backpressure observed on the audit topic: producers are filling the Kafka partitions when ES indexing slows. Short-term mitigation: increase producer batching and switch consumer to bulk write into ClickHouse for hot-path analytics, while async indexing to ES.

maria: Here's a tiny schema diff we discussed:

```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "action": "string",
  "resource": {"id": "string", "type": "string"},
  "policy_id": "string",
  "policy_version": "string",
  "outcome": "allow|deny|error",
  "meta": "object"  // small ext-field, avoid huge nested policy blobs
}
```

maria: note: keep `meta` limited by size (256 bytes) to prevent explosion in index and cost.

auditsrv-bot: ingest-latency WARNING: avg ack latency for audit-topic = 420ms (threshold 200ms)

sam: For backpressure, we could add adaptive routing: if ES backlog > X and tenant not flagged for full capture, route events to cold storage and emit a lightweight indexed event `archived:true` so search shows placeholder. That keeps user-facing audit search consistent (shows event exists) without full body.

jason: Implementation details: producer side add `X-accepts-archived` header on tenant config; consumers check header and short-circuit heavy enrichment. Also add a circuit-breaker on consumer with exponential backoff and a histogram metric for requeue counts.

maria: Curious about cost math: any quick estimate for KMS+ES vs DEK flow?

sam: Rough back-of-envelope: KMS sign ~ $0.0003 per call. At 100M events/month that’s $30k. DEK rotation monthly with KMS calls ~ 10 calls = <$0.01. ES storage + indexing is dominant though; indexing tokenization/field mappings for high-cardinality `resource.id` and `policy_id` may add 2-5x to ES bill compared to storing raw blobs in cold storage.

katie: For compliance requests, SLA is 24 hours for full event retrieval. So archive + on-demand expansion meets that. For incidents, we still need hot-path full events for last 7 days. So per-tenant retention tiers: hot 7d, warm 30d, cold 365d.

maria: For validation: customers want schema validation failures surfaced in their dashboards. We should add a `validation_status` field with enums: `valid | partial | invalid` and include `validation_errors` (small array of strings). Invalid events should not be dropped if critical; instead mark and route to quarantine topic.

sam: Quarantine topic + triage process sounds right. Add an alert if quarantine rate > 0.5% for a tenant.

jason: Operationally, we should also shard ES by tenant-hash to avoid one tenant blowing up indexing. For very high-cardinality workloads, prefer ClickHouse for querying aggregates and S3 for full event retrieval.

maria: I'll draft a runbook: steps for (1) rotate to DEK envelope signing, (2) migrate policy blobs to S3 snapshot table, (3) implement `archived` routing and `validation_status`, (4) per-tenant quota + sampling.

katie: Can you tag me when ready? customers in compliance pipeline want this before EOM.

maria: tagging @katie — will post PR and runbook later today.

auditsrv-bot: deploy-bot INFO: canary deploy audit-archiver v2 starting in infra-canary

sam: Nice. Also: add a simple schema diff-checker that rejects changes that would increase index cardinality without an opt-in flag. We had a surprise yesterday where a new `resource.path` free-text field caused a 3x ES index growth.

maria: Good call. I'll include that in the PR: schema change gating + migration plan.

katie: Thanks all. short-term action items: maria PR, jason telemetry for consumer backpressure, sam cost estimate for DEK vs KMS, security to review key rotation plan.

maria: on it.
